question: A manufacturing company produces three types of electronic components: A, B, and C. The company has four different production lines, each capable of producing these components with varying efficiencies. Each worker on line 2 can produce 8 units of component A, 10 units of component B, and 12 units of component C per hour. Each worker on line 3 can produce 12 units of component A, 6 units of component B, and 10 units of component C per hour. Each worker on line 4 can produce 15 units of component A, 8 units of component B, and 5 units of component C per hour. The company needs to produce at least 1000 units of component A, 800 units of component B, and 1200 units of component C daily. The production lines can only be operated if at least 5 workers are assigned. Please determine the minimum production time to meet the daily demand. There are total 50 workers available. Each production line can be utilized by up to 15 workers at a time. Each production line must have at least 5 workers to operate. Each worker on line 1 can produce 10 units of component A, 5 units of component B, and 15 units of component C per hour.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "lines": [1, 2, 3, 4],
    "components": ["A", "B", "C"],
    # units produced per worker-hour: rate[line][component]
    "rate": {
        1: {"A": 10, "B": 5,  "C": 15},
        2: {"A": 8,  "B": 10, "C": 12},
        3: {"A": 12, "B": 6,  "C": 10},
        4: {"A": 15, "B": 8,  "C": 5},
    },
    "demand": {"A": 1000, "B": 800, "C": 1200},
    "total_workers": 50,
    "min_workers_per_line": 5,
    "max_workers_per_line": 15,
    "big_m": 10000,
}

GOLD_ANSWER = None


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.L = pyo.Set(initialize=d["lines"], ordered=True)
    model.C = pyo.Set(initialize=d["components"], ordered=True)

    # w[l]: workers assigned to line l (0 if line off, else 5..15)
    model.w = pyo.Var(
        model.L, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=(0, d["max_workers_per_line"]),
    )
    # y[l]: 1 if line l operates
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.L, domain=pyo.Binary)
    # h[l]: worker-hours used on line l
    model.h = pyo.Var(model.L, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    # T: overall production time (makespan), hours
    model.T = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Objective: minimise total production time
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.T, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Demand for each component: sum_l rate[l][c] * h[l] >= demand[c]
    def demand_rule(m, c):
        return sum(d["rate"][l][c] * m.h[l] for l in m.L) >= d["demand"][c]
    model.demand_con = pyo.Constraint(model.C, rule=demand_rule)

    # Total workers across lines <= 50
    def workers_rule(m):
        return sum(m.w[l] for l in m.L) <= d["total_workers"]
    model.workers_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=workers_rule)

    # Operating linkage: min_workers*y[l] <= w[l] <= max_workers*y[l]
    def minw_rule(m, l):
        return d["min_workers_per_line"] * m.y[l] <= m.w[l]
    model.minw_con = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=minw_rule)

    def maxw_rule(m, l):
        return m.w[l] <= d["max_workers_per_line"] * m.y[l]
    model.maxw_con = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=maxw_rule)

    # worker-hours cannot exceed (max workers) * T (time available)
    def hours_time_rule(m, l):
        return m.h[l] <= d["max_workers_per_line"] * m.T
    model.hours_time_con = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=hours_time_rule)

    # worker-hours only if operating: h[l] <= bigM * y[l]
    def hours_on_rule(m, l):
        return m.h[l] <= d["big_m"] * m.y[l]
    model.hours_on_con = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=hours_on_rule)

    # worker-hours cannot exceed workers assigned * T (worker-hours feasibility)
    # w[l]*T is bilinear, so reinforce with h[l] <= max_workers * T above
    # and h[l] <= w[l] * bigM via workers (kept linear)
    def hours_workers_rule(m, l):
        return m.h[l] <= d["max_workers_per_line"] * d["big_m"] * m.y[l]
    model.hours_workers_con = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=hours_workers_rule)

    return model

        ) >= d["demand"][p]

    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=demand_rule)

    # If operated, at least min workers; if not operated, zero workers
    def operate_lb_rule(m, l):

    model.operate_lb = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=operate_lb_rule)

        return m.workers[l] <= d["max_workers_per_line"] * m.operate[l]

    model.operate_ub = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=operate_ub_rule)

    # Makespan linking: worker-hours on a line cannot exceed max workers * T
    def makespan_rule(m, l):
        return m.worker_hours[l] <= d["max_workers_per_line"] * m.T

    model.makespan = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=makespan_rule)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Structured formulation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sets / indices
#   LINES      = {1,2,3,4}          production lines
#   COMPONENTS = {"A","B","C"}      electronic components
#
# Decision variables
#   x[i]  : integer, 0..15   workers assigned to line i
#   y[i]  : binary          1 if line i is operated (>= 5 workers), else 0
#   t     : nonnegative real production time (hours), shared by all lines
#
# Objective (minimise)
#   Minimise total production time t.
#
# Constraints
#   (1) Line activation lower bound:  x[i] >= 5 * y[i]        (source: "must have at least 5 workers to operate")
#   (2) Line activation upper bound:  x[i] <= 15 * y[i]       (source: "up to 15 workers at a time")
#   (3) Total workforce:              sum_i x[i] <= 50        (source: "total 50 workers available")
#   (4) Demand satisfaction:          sum_i rate[i,j] * x[i] * t >= demand[j]
#       The product x[i]*t is bilinear.  It is linearised exactly by
#       introducing w[i] = x[i] * t with the standard big-M envelope:
#           w[i] <= 15 * t
#           w[i] <= TMAX * x[i]
#           w[i] >= TMAX * x[i] - TMAX * 15 * (1 - y[i])
#           w[i] >= 0
#       and replacing x[i]*t by w[i] in the demand constraints.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    "LINES": [1, 2, 3, 4],
    "COMPONENTS": ["A", "B", "C"],
    # rate[line][component] = units produced per worker per hour
    "rate": {
        1: {"A": 10, "B": 5,  "C": 15},
        2: {"A": 8,  "B": 10, "C": 12},
        3: {"A": 12, "B": 6,  "C": 10},
        4: {"A": 15, "B": 8,  "C": 5},
    },
    "demand": {"A": 1000, "B": 800, "C": 1200},
    "min_workers_per_line": 5,
    "max_workers_per_line": 15,
    "total_workers": 50,
    "TMAX": 1000,   # big-M upper bound on production time (hours)
}

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.LINES = pyo.Set(initialize=d["LINES"])
    model.COMPONENTS = pyo.Set(initialize=d["COMPONENTS"])

    # Decision variables
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.LINES,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=(0, d["max_workers_per_line"]),
    )
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.LINES, domain=pyo.Binary)
    model.t = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["TMAX"]))
    model.w = pyo.Var(model.LINES, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # (1) lower activation bound
    def lower_activation_rule(m, i):
        return m.x[i] >= d["min_workers_per_line"] * m.y[i]
    model.lower_activation = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=lower_activation_rule)

    # (2) upper activation bound
    def upper_activation_rule(m, i):
        return m.x[i] <= d["max_workers_per_line"] * m.y[i]
    model.upper_activation = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=upper_activation_rule)

    # (3) total workforce
    def total_workers_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[i] for i in m.LINES) <= d["total_workers"]
    model.total_workers = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_workers_rule)

    # Linearisation of w[i] = x[i] * t
    def w_upper_t_rule(m, i):
        return m.w[i] <= d["max_workers_per_line"] * m.t
    model.w_upper_t = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=w_upper_t_rule)

    def w_upper_x_rule(m, i):
        return m.w[i] <= d["TMAX"] * m.x[i]
    model.w_upper_x = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=w_upper_x_rule)

    def w_lower_rule(m, i):
        return (
            m.w[i]
            >= d["TMAX"] * m.x[i]
            - d["TMAX"] * d["max_workers_per_line"] * (1 - m.y[i])
        )
    model.w_lower = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=w_lower_rule)

    # (4) demand satisfaction
    def demand_rule(m, j):
        return (
            sum(d["rate"][i][j] * m.w[i] for i in m.LINES)
            >= d["demand"][j]
        )
    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(model.COMPONENTS, rule=demand_rule)

    # Objective
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.t, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.LINES = pyo.Set(initialize=d["lines"])
    model.PROD = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"])

    # t = common production time (hours) for the whole plant
    model.t = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # w[i] = worker-hours spent on line i  (= workers_i * t)
    model.w = pyo.Var(model.LINES, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["big_m"]))

    # y[i] = 1 if line i is operated, else 0
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.LINES, domain=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize production time

    def lower_rule(m, i):

            - d["big_m"] * (1 - m.y[i])
    model.lower_wh = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=lower_rule)

    # (b) worker-hours <= 15*t (up to 15 workers)

    model.upper_wh = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=upper_wh_rule)

    # (c) if line off, worker-hours = 0
    def off_rule(m, i):
        return m.w[i] <= d["big_m"] * m.y[i]
    model.off_link = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=off_rule)

    # (d) total workers used over horizon <= 50 * t
    def total_workers_rule(m):
        return sum(m.w[i] for i in m.LINES) <= d["total_workers"] * m.t
    model.total_workers = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_workers_rule)

    # (e) meet demand for each product
    def demand_rule(m, p):
        return sum(d["rate"][p][i] * m.w[i] for i in m.LINES) >= d["demand"][p]
    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(model.PROD, rule=demand_rule)

    return model

    "rate": {
        1: {"A": 10, "B": 5,  "C": 15},

        2: {"A": 8,  "B": 10, "C": 12},

        3: {"A": 12, "B": 6,  "C": 10},
        # "Each worker on line 4 can produce 15 units of component A, 8 units of component B, and 5 units of component C per hour."
        4: {"A": 15, "B": 8,  "C": 5},
    },
    # "...needs to produce at least 1000 units of component A, 800 units of component B, and 1200 units of component C daily."
    "demand": {"A": 1000, "B": 800, "C": 1200},
    # "There are total 50 workers available."
    "total_workers": 50,
    # "Each production line can be utilized by up to 15 workers at a time."
    "max_workers_per_line": 15,
    # "Each production line must have at least 5 workers to operate."
    "min_workers_per_line": 5,
    # big-M for time (upper bound on operating hours per line per day, chosen safely large)
    "bigM_time": 1000.0,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    lines = sorted(d["rate"].keys())
    comps = sorted(d["demand"].keys())
    kmax = d["max_workers_per_line"]
    kset = list(range(0, kmax + 1))

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    m.L = pyo.Set(initialize=lines, ordered=True)
    m.P = pyo.Set(initialize=comps, ordered=True)
    m.K = pyo.Set(initialize=kset, ordered=True)

    # y[L] = 1 if line L is operated at all
    m.y = pyo.Var(m.L, within=pyo.Binary)

    # z[L,k] = 1 if exactly k workers are assigned to line L
    m.z = pyo.Var(m.L, m.K, within=pyo.Binary)

    # t[L] = hours line L operates
    m.t = pyo.Var(m.L, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["bigM_time"]))

    # v[L,k] = z[L,k] * t[L]  (linearisation of the product of binary and continuous)
    m.v = pyo.Var(m.L, m.K, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["bigM_time"]))

    # T = makespan (objective)
    m.T = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["bigM_time"]))

    # Exactly one worker-count value is selected per line
    def one_count_rule(mm, L):
        return sum(mm.z[L, k] for k in mm.K) == 1
    m.one_count = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=one_count_rule)

    # y[L] = 1 iff count >= 1 (count is 0 only when y=0)
    def operate_rule(mm, L):
        return mm.z[L, 0] == 1 - mm.y[L]
    m.operate = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=operate_rule)

    # If operated, worker count must be >= min_workers_per_line
    def min_workers_rule(mm, L):
        return sum(k * mm.z[L, k] for k in mm.K) >= d["min_workers_per_line"] * mm.y[L]
    m.min_workers = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=min_workers_rule)

    # McCormick linearisation of v[L,k] = z[L,k] * t[L]
    def v_le_t_rule(mm, L, k):
        return mm.v[L, k] <= mm.t[L]
    m.v_le_t = pyo.Constraint(m.L, m.K, rule=v_le_t_rule)

    def v_le_Mz_rule(mm, L, k):
        return mm.v[L, k] <= d["bigM_time"] * mm.z[L, k]
    m.v_le_Mz = pyo.Constraint(m.L, m.K, rule=v_le_Mz_rule)

    def v_ge_t_minus_M_rule(mm, L, k):
        return mm.v[L, k] >= mm.t[L] - d["bigM_time"] * (1 - mm.z[L, k])
    m.v_ge_t_minus_M = pyo.Constraint(m.L, m.K, rule=v_ge_t_minus_M_rule)

    # Hours on any operating line cannot exceed the makespan
    def hours_le_T_rule(mm, L):
        return mm.t[L] <= mm.T
    m.hours_le_T = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=hours_le_T_rule)

    # If a line is not operated, its hours must be zero
    def hours_off_rule(mm, L):
        return mm.t[L] <= d["bigM_time"] * mm.y[L]
    m.hours_off = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=hours_off_rule)

    # Total workers used across all lines <= total available
    def total_workers_rule(mm):
        return sum(k * mm.z[L, k] for L in mm.L for k in mm.K) <= d["total_workers"]
    m.total_workers = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_workers_rule)

    # Production demand for each component
    # production on line L for component p = rate[L,p] * (workers on L) * (hours on L)
    #                                     = rate[L,p] * sum_k k * v[L,k]
    def demand_rule(mm, p):
        return sum(
            d["rate"][L][p] * sum(k * mm.v[L, k] for k in mm.K)
            for L in mm.L
        ) >= d["demand"][p]
    m.demand = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=demand_rule)

    # Objective: minimise makespan
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.T, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return m

DATA = {
    "lines": [1, 2, 3, 4],
    "components": ["A", "B", "C"],

        4: {"A": 15, "B": 8,  "C": 5},
    },
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.L = pyo.Set(initialize=d["lines"])
    m.Cm = pyo.Set(initialize=d["components"])

    # Decision variables
    m.workers = pyo.Var(m.L, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                        bounds=(0, d["w_max"]))
    m.hours = pyo.Var(m.L, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    m.run = pyo.Var(m.L, domain=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize total production time (sum of line operating hours)
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=sum(m.hours[l] for l in m.L), sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Total workers available
    def total_workers_rule(m):
        return sum(m.workers[l] for l in m.L) <= d["workers_total"]
    m.total_workers = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_workers_rule)

    # Line operates only if at least w_min workers assigned
    def min_workers_rule(m, l):
        return m.workers[l] >= d["w_min"] * m.run[l]
    m.min_workers = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=min_workers_rule)

    # Line can be utilized by up to w_max workers (already bounded, but enforce via run)
    def max_workers_rule(m, l):
        return m.workers[l] <= d["w_max"] * m.run[l]
    m.max_workers = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=max_workers_rule)

    # Hours only when line is running (big-M)
    def hours_on_rule(m, l):
        return m.hours[l] <= d["M_h"] * m.run[l]
    m.hours_on = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=hours_on_rule)

    # Demand constraints: sum over lines of workers*rate*hours >= demand
    # workers*hours is nonlinear, so we linearise using a per-line "worker-hours" variable.
    # Introduce labour[l] = workers[l] * hours[l] via McCormick-style linearisation is not
    # exact for products of two variables. Instead, we treat the product as a single
    # decision variable "worker_hours" and link it linearly to workers and hours using
    # the fact that hours is bounded by M_h and workers by w_max.
    #
    # To keep the model strictly linear and exact, we instead fix the interpretation:
    # each line runs for a common production time T (hours), and workers are assigned
    # per line. Then worker-hours = workers[l] * T is still nonlinear.
    #
    # The clean linear formulation: let x[l] = workers[l] * hours[l] (worker-hours).
    # We linearise x[l] = workers[l] * hours[l] with binary run and bounds:
    #   x[l] <= w_max * hours[l]
    #   x[l] <= M_h * workers[l]
    #   x[l] >= w_min * hours[l] - M_h * w_min * (1 - run[l])
    #   x[l] >= 0
    # This is a standard linearisation of a bilinear term when one factor is bounded
    # and the other is bounded, using the big-M method with the run indicator.
    m.worker_hours = pyo.Var(m.L, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    def wh_upper_hours_rule(m, l):
        return m.worker_hours[l] <= d["w_max"] * m.hours[l]
    m.wh_upper_hours = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=wh_upper_hours_rule)

    def wh_upper_workers_rule(m, l):
        return m.worker_hours[l] <= d["M_h"] * m.workers[l]
    m.wh_upper_workers = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=wh_upper_workers_rule)

    def wh_lower_rule(m, l):
        return m.worker_hours[l] >= d["w_min"] * m.hours[l] - d["M_h"] * d["w_min"] * (1 - m.run[l])
    m.wh_lower = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=wh_lower_rule)

    # Demand constraints using worker_hours
    def demand_rule(m, c):
        return sum(d["rate"][l][c] * m.worker_hours[l] for l in m.L) >= d["demand"][c]

    # by treating production as eff[l][c] * n[l] * t[l] which is bilinear.
    # To keep the model linear, we replace the product n[l]*t[l] with a
    # new variable w[l] = n[l] * t[l] and linearise using McCormick envelopes.
    m.w = pyo.Var(m.lines, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.Tmax, sense=pyo.minimize)

    "max_hours": 1000,
}


def build_model(data=None):

    lines = d["lines"]
    comps = d["components"]
    rate = d["rate"]
    demand = d["demand"]
    W = d["total_workers"]
    wmin = d["min_workers_per_line"]
    wmax = d["max_workers_per_line"]
    Hmax = d["max_hours"]

    model.COMPONENTS = pyo.Set(initialize=comps)

        model.LINES,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=(0, wmax),
    )

    # binary: line is operated (requires >= wmin workers)
    model.operates = pyo.Var(model.LINES, within=pyo.Binary)

    # hours each line runs
    model.hours = pyo.Var(
        model.LINES,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        bounds=(0, Hmax),
    )

    # makespan / total production time
    model.T = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, Hmax))

    # worker-hours per line = workers[l] * hours[l]  (linearised)
    model.worker_hours = pyo.Var(
        model.LINES,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        bounds=(0, wmax * Hmax),
    )

    # total units of each component produced
    model.produced = pyo.Var(model.COMPONENTS, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # ---- Objective: minimise total production time ----
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.T, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ---- Worker count linked to operation (5..15 if operated, else 0) ----
    def worker_lb_rule(m, l):
        return m.workers[l] >= wmin * m.operates[l]

    def worker_ub_rule(m, l):
        return m.workers[l] <= wmax * m.operates[l]

    model.worker_lb = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=worker_lb_rule)
    model.worker_ub = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=worker_ub_rule)

    # ---- Total workers available ----
    def total_workers_rule(m):
        return sum(m.workers[l] for l in m.LINES) <= W

    model.total_workers = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_workers_rule)

    # ---- Makespan: each line's hours <= T ----
    def makespan_rule(m, l):
        return m.hours[l] <= m.T

    model.makespan = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=makespan_rule)

    # ---- Linearise worker_hours = workers * hours (McCormick) ----
    # workers in [0, wmax], hours in [0, Hmax]
    def wh_lb1_rule(m, l):
        return m.worker_hours[l] >= 0

    def wh_ub1_rule(m, l):
        return m.worker_hours[l] <= wmax * m.hours[l]

    def wh_ub2_rule(m, l):
        return m.worker_hours[l] <= Hmax * m.workers[l]

    def wh_lb2_rule(m, l):
        return m.worker_hours[l] >= (
            wmax * m.hours[l] + Hmax * m.workers[l] - wmax * Hmax
        )

    model.wh_lb1 = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=wh_lb1_rule)
    model.wh_ub1 = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=wh_ub1_rule)
    model.wh_ub2 = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=wh_ub2_rule)
    model.wh_lb2 = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=wh_lb2_rule)

    # ---- Production of each component = sum over lines of rate * worker_hours ----
    def produced_rule(m, c):
        return m.produced[c] == sum(
            rate[l][c] * m.worker_hours[l] for l in m.LINES
        )

    model.produced_def = pyo.Constraint(model.COMPONENTS, rule=produced_rule)

    # ---- Demand satisfaction ----
    def demand_rule(m, c):
        return m.produced[c] >= demand[c]

    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(model.COMPONENTS, rule=demand_rule)

    return model

subject to meeting the daily component demands.

(2) Demand B:  sum_i rate[i][1] * wk[i] * hop[i] >= demand[1]
(3) Demand C:  sum_i rate[i][2] * wk[i] * hop[i] >= demand[2]
(4) Makespan:  hop[i] <= T                       for all i
(5) Min workers if used:  wk[i] >= WMIN * use[i] for all i
(6) Max workers if used:  wk[i] <= WMAX * use[i] for all i
(7) Total workers:        sum_i wk[i] <= WTOTAL

Linearisation of the bilinear term wk[i]*hop[i]
-----------------------------------------------
The product of an integer worker count and a continuous time is bilinear.
We linearise it with a standard McCormick / big-M disaggregation using
binary expansion of the worker count.  Since wk[i] is bounded by WMAX,
we introduce binary variables z[i,k] for k = 1..WMAX with
    wk[i] = sum_k z[i,k]
and continuous variables q[i,k] = z[i,k] * hop[i], linearised by
    q[i,k] <= HMAX * z[i,k]
    q[i,k] <= hop[i]
    q[i,k] >= hop[i] - HMAX * (1 - z[i,k])
    q[i,k] >= 0

DATA = {
    # rate[i][j] : units of component j per worker-hour on line i
    "rate": [

    ],
    "demand": [1000, 800, 1200],   # A, B, C
    "WMIN": 5,
    "WMAX": 15,
    "WTOTAL": 50,
    "HMAX": 1000.0,   # big-M horizon bound on operating hours
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    n_lines = len(d["rate"])
    n_comp = len(d["demand"])
    WMAX = d["WMAX"]
    WMIN = d["WMIN"]
    WTOTAL = d["WTOTAL"]
    HMAX = d["HMAX"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ---- Sets -------------------------------------------------------------
    model.I = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_lines - 1)
    model.J = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_comp - 1)
    model.K = pyo.RangeSet(1, WMAX)

    # ---- Variables --------------------------------------------------------
    model.wk = pyo.Var(model.I, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                       bounds=(0, WMAX))
    model.use = pyo.Var(model.I, within=pyo.Binary)
    model.hop = pyo.Var(model.I, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
                        bounds=(0, HMAX))
    model.T = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, HMAX))

    # binary expansion of worker count and disaggregated hours
    model.z = pyo.Var(model.I, model.K, within=pyo.Binary)
    model.q = pyo.Var(model.I, model.K, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
                      bounds=(0, HMAX))

    # ---- Constraints ------------------------------------------------------

    # (1)-(3) demand constraints, linearised via q
    def demand_rule(m, j):
        return sum(d["rate"][i][j] * m.q[i, k]
                   for i in m.I for k in m.K) >= d["demand"][j]
    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=demand_rule)

    # (4) makespan: hop[i] <= T
    def makespan_rule(m, i):
        return m.hop[i] <= m.T
    model.makespan = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=makespan_rule)

    # (5) min workers if used
    def minworkers_rule(m, i):
        return m.wk[i] >= WMIN * m.use[i]
    model.minworkers = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=minworkers_rule)

    # (6) max workers if used
    def maxworkers_rule(m, i):
        return m.wk[i] <= WMAX * m.use[i]
    model.maxworkers = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=maxworkers_rule)

    # (7) total workers
    def totalworkers_rule(m):
        return sum(m.wk[i] for i in m.I) <= WTOTAL
    model.totalworkers = pyo.Constraint(rule=totalworkers_rule)

    # worker count equals sum of binary expansion
    def wkdef_rule(m, i):
        return m.wk[i] == sum(m.z[i, k] for k in m.K)
    model.wkdef = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=wkdef_rule)

    # McCormick linearisation of q[i,k] = z[i,k] * hop[i]
    def q_upper1_rule(m, i, k):
        return m.q[i, k] <= HMAX * m.z[i, k]
    model.q_upper1 = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.K, rule=q_upper1_rule)

    def q_upper2_rule(m, i, k):
        return m.q[i, k] <= m.hop[i]
    model.q_upper2 = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.K, rule=q_upper2_rule)

    def q_lower_rule(m, i, k):
        return m.q[i, k] >= m.hop[i] - HMAX * (1 - m.z[i, k])
    model.q_lower = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.K, rule=q_lower_rule)

    # ---- Objective --------------------------------------------------------
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.T, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model
